correctness.rationale: For every finite simple undirected graph, graphic edge closure is connectivity closure. For a chordless cycle C, the rooted path E(C)\{e} is minimally nonclosed, adds exactly e, and every proper subset is closed. Chord-splitting induction derives any missing edge from induced-cycle rules; the first nontrivial application excludes all other pseudo-intents under their recursive definition. Minimal nonclosed premises force each canonical implication in every sound complete basis. For one simultaneous pass, a simple path joining endpoints of e is a minimal stem; one rooted all-cycle rule per stem is forced in a direct-unit basis. DG direct iff all simple cycles induced; maximal premise size<=2 iff graph chordal; finite disconnected/acyclic cases are included. K_n cycle counts yield 3*C(n,3) versus n!/2*sum_{j=0}^{n-3}1/j!; wheel rim r>=4 has r hub triangles and one induced rim giving 4r. An independently written checker enumerated all 1096 simple graphs on 3–5 vertices and all 59805 edge subsets, comparing DSU closure, recursively computed pseudo-intents, induced-cycle rules, all rooted simple-cycle direct rules; all passed. K_n orders 3–6 and wheels r4–7 count identities checked. The finite checks are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Prior published mathematics decisively covers the structural claim by implication. Wild (arXiv:1411.6432, full text Sections 3.3 and 4.1.4, referencing original 1994 theorem) establishes both the unique optimum basis consisting of closed circuits for ALL binary matroids, explicitly including graphic matroids, and universal minimum one-pass direct bases made from all closure stems. Closed graphic circuits are exactly induced cycles, whereas missing-edge stems are exactly rooted simple paths. Kashiwabara–Nakamura 2013 separately explicitly identifies chordless graphic prime stems and proves them pseudo-closed. The remaining chordality test and the K_n factorial-vs-cubic enumeration are immediate specializations and elementary graph-cycle counts. Exact same wording/formula need not be previously printed for a covered corollary. Thus O FAIL, despite an independently correct proof; this is not a rejection based merely on limited literature access.
